findings.description: The new WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS loader falls back to ("general-purpose") whenever the array is empty, without distinguishing why it is empty. The header comment and SC-T-AGENT-9 describe the fallback as applying to 'a missing or unparsable file', but a present, well-formed agent-types.yaml in which every entry is write_capable: false (or in which .agent_types has no entries) also triggers it, silently re-enabling general-purpose for write-capable skills. The same branch swallows a missing `yq` binary or a yq syntax incompatibility (2>/dev/null || true) with no diagnostic, so the only visible symptom is the validator rejecting every `agent: claude` / `agent: fork` write skill with an error that lists only '(general-purpose)'. Note: the diff attributes this hunk to a `new file` header for .claude/data/agent-types.yaml, but the content is the validator script; the real path was not in the diff, so the anchor is by hunk header.
findings.failure_mode: An operator who edits agent-types.yaml to mark general-purpose write_capable: false with no other true entries expects general-purpose to be rejected, but the validator accepts it. Separately, on a CI host without yq (or with the Python yq wrapper, where `yq eval` fails), skills that legitimately set agent: claude or agent: fork fail validation with a misleading message and no indication that the data file was never read.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture yq's exit status separately from the result: run yq into a variable, fall back to general-purpose only when the file is absent or yq exited non-zero, and honour an empty parsed set as 'no agent may be named'. Emit a one-line stderr warning when the fallback is taken (e.g. 'agent-types.yaml unreadable; using built-in default general-purpose') so the misconfiguration is visible in CI logs. Add a test for the all-false file case to pin whichever semantics are intended.

findings.description: agent-types.yaml is now the single source of truth for which agent types have Write/Edit, but nothing verifies that its write_capable flags agree with the agent definitions they describe. SC-T-AGENT-7 asserts that every .claude/agents/*.md has a row and pins the exact current key/value string, but it does not read each agent's `tools:` frontmatter and compare. The invariant behind Issue #553 is precisely that a skill declaring write capability must not be bound to an agent whose allowlist lacks Write/Edit; with the flag now a hand-maintained boolean, a one-line edit to either file can desynchronise them and the test suite stays green.
findings.failure_mode: A future change marks a project agent write_capable: true in the YAML (or adds Write to an agent's tools without updating the YAML, or vice versa). In the fail-open direction, a skill with write_files: true and agent: <that type> passes validate-skill-capabilities.sh, then fails silently at runtime because the agent cannot call Write/Edit, which is the exact #553 symptom this mechanism exists to prevent. The hard-coded exact-string assertion also means every new agent file requires an unrelated test edit, encouraging reviewers to update the string reflexively rather than check the flag.
findings.suggested_fix: In SC-T-AGENT-7 (or a new SC-T-AGENT-10), for each .claude/agents/*.md parse the frontmatter `tools:` list and assert that `write_capable` equals whether Write or Edit appears in it; keep the harness-only types (general-purpose, claude, fork, Plan, Explore) as the explicitly enumerated exceptions. Replace the brittle exact-string equality with per-key assertions so adding an agent file only requires the derived check to pass.
